role: One open hold per disposition that requires a successor. A hold names where the requirement came from, the canon subject or record it concerns, the predecessor closures it qualifies, and what a successor must do to discharge it.
rule: Append-only. Hold identities are seeded from their named sources and are never rewritten or reordered; the sequence is dense. A hold's state changes only by appending to its own state_transitions, and `state` is the last transition's target, written by tooling and re-derived on every check.
projection_directive: While a hold is open, every predecessor record it names MUST project as verified_historical_with_open_successor and MUST NOT project as unqualified verified. A projection is not permitted to round the qualification off.
claim_boundary: A hold records an owed successor and nothing else. Opening one asserts no defect in the predecessor's original proof, changes no status, and closes no stage. Discharging one asserts only that a successor was admitted — the successor's own proof is the successor's own obligation.

successor_graph_model.why: required_successor.work_item_id is SINGULAR. osh-0001 qualifies seven verified closures whose re-proofs are genuinely different work, so the singular field left only two shapes: open a second hold over the same disposition, which double-counts one requirement, or merge two proof contracts into one successor, so neither is proven on its own terms. The owner refused both and directed that the MODEL be corrected instead. Hold identities, hold count, and every existing hold body are unchanged; one optional block was added inside required_successor.

shape.aggregate: MUST equal required_successor.work_item_id. The graph's root and the hold's singular successor reference are the same thing.
shape.subordinate_proofs: One entry per qualified predecessor that has a named successor: {work_item_id, re_proves_predecessor}.
shape.outstanding_predecessors: One entry per qualified predecessor that is owed and unwritten: {predecessor, why}. Naming them is what stops a partial graph reporting itself complete.

rejections: hold-graph-root-mismatch — the graph root disagrees with required_successor.work_item_id
hold-graph-aggregate-unknown — the root is not a record
hold-graph-aggregate-not-an-aggregate — the root is not an aggregate_exit
hold-graph-subordinate-unknown — a subordinate is not a record
hold-graph-subordinate-unjoined — the aggregate does not join a subordinate the graph names
hold-graph-predecessor-uncovered — a qualified closure appears in neither list, or in both
hold-discharge-graph-incomplete — discharge attempted while a subordinate is unproven or anything is outstanding
successor_graph_model.claim_boundary: The graph records what is owed and how it is apportioned. It proves nothing, admits nothing, and discharges nothing.
